Literacy rate among musllm women 
*423. SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM : Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to. state: 
(a) whether the literacy rate among Muslim women is growing in 
India; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. SANJAY PASWAN): (a) to (c) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) As per census 2001, the Female Literacy rate has increased 
by 14.8 percentage points, i.e. 39.3% in 1991 to 54.16% in 2001. 
According to the Registrar General of India, the data pertaining to the 
literacy rate among Muslim women as per 2001 Census is not available. 
However, as per the National Samp le Survey Organization (NSSO) 55th 
Round 1999-2000, the Muslim female literacy rate of the country is 
62.2% for Urban areas and 42.1% for Rural areas. Table indicating the 
State-wise Muslim female literacy rate (Rural and Urban) is enclosed.

RAJYA SABHA [22 August, 2003] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. SANJAY PASWAN): (a) to (e) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (e) The Government of India has approved a new programme 
called 'National Programme for Education of Girls at Elementary Level 
(NPEGEL)' as an amendment to the existing scheme of Sarva Shiksha 
Abhiyan (SSA) for providing additional components for education of girls 
at elementary level. The NPEGEL will form part of SSA and will be 
implemented under the umbrella of SSA but with a distinct identity. 
The scheme would provide the following additional components under 
SSA:— (i) to develop a school at cluster level, as a model girl-child friendly 
school; (ii) additional incentives such as stationery, slates, work books, 
uniforms and/or to meet any other locally felt need within the existing 
ceiling of Rs. 1507-per child per annum; (iii) additional interventions like 
awards to schools/teachers, student evaluation, remedial teaching, bridge 
courses, alternative schools, learning through open schools, teacher 
training and child care centres at the cl uster level within a ceiling of Rs. 
60,000/ per annum; (iv) mobilisation and community monitoring within a 
ceiling of Rs. 95,000/- per cluster over a five-year period (v) development 
of materials; as well as (vi) planning, training and management support. 
For implementation of the above pr ogramme an estimated expenditure 
amounting to Rs. 1064.80 crores has been kept for the Tenth plan period. 
The scheme is slated for implementation from 25th Septemeber, 2003. 
The Scheme will be implemented in Educationally Backward Blocks 
(EBBs) where the level of rural female literacy is less than the national 
average and the gender gap is above the national average, in blocks of 
districts which are not covered under EBBs but are having atleast 5% 
SC/ST population and where SC/ST female literacy is below 10% and 
also in select urban slums. Based on 1991 Census data, the scheme 
would cover Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, 
Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Prades h, Karnataka, Jammu and Kashmir, 
Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, 
Orissa, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Na du, Uttar Pradesh, Uttaranchal and 
West Bengal. Once the data for 2001 Census become available, selection 
of blocks will be modified according to the revised data.

†*428.  SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH 'LALAN': †† 
   SHRI KAPIL SIBAL : 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to 
state : 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Supreme Court has directed 
Government to recover immediately 50 per cent of amount from drug 
companies on account of overcharging from consumers for the drugs; 
(b) if so, the details of such drug manufacturers and amount 
overcharged by each of them from consumers; and 
(c) the action taken to recover 50 per cent of the said amount? 
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI SUKH 
DEV SINGH DHINDSA) : (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of 
the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) The Supreme Court in the appeals by the Government 
against the judgment of the Bombay High Court excluding Ciprofloxacin, 
Doxycycline, Glipizide, Salbutamol, Theophylline, Norfloxacin and 
Cloxacillin from price control, passed an order, on the 1st August, 2003, 
inter-alia, setting aside the judgment of the High Court and holding. "We 
also consider it just and proper to give liberty to the appellant and the 
concerned statutory authorities to recover 50% of the 'overcharged' 
amounts pending fresh determination by the High Court. Accordingly, we 
direct stay of recovery of 50% of the 'overcharged' amount subject to the 
payment of remaining 50% within the period of four weeks from the date 
of communication of the amount payable by each of the writ petitioners." 
The respondent companies in the appeals were M/s Cipla Limited, 
M/s USV Ltd., M/s Raj Medicals, M/s Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd., 
M/s Unichem Laboratories Ltd., M/s Okasa Ltd., M/s Okasa Pharma 
Ltd. etc. The overcharged amount is determined by deducting the 
assessed notional revenue that would have accrued on the basis of the 
volume of sales at the price fixed under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 
1995 provisions from the assessed actual revenue earned.

†430. SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the attention of Government has been drawn towards 
commodities sold on stations and in trains by unauthorised vendors due 
to which travellers have to face lot of difficulties and incidents of theft 
etc. often take place; 
(b) if so, whether Government have formulated any scheme against 
those unauthorised vendors including the steps to implement it; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI 
BANDARU DATTATRAYA): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of 
the House. 
Statement 
(a) Yes, Sir. Government is aware of the unauthorised vending/ 
hawking in trains and at railway stations. 
(b) and (c) Unauthorised vending/hawking is an offence under the 
provision of Section 144 of the Railways Act, 1989.To iradicate the nuisance 
of unauthorised vending/hawking causi ng inconvenience to the passengers, 
regular drives are being conducted against them is co-ordination with 
commercial staff and Government Railway Police personnel. 
During the year 2002,71,406 persons were prosecuted u/s 144 of the 
Railways Act, 1989 and 57,441 persons were convicted for unauthorised 
vending and an amount of Rs. 1,61,59,421/- was realised as fine.

developed by M/s. MAYHCO in March, 2002 for a period of three years

of bollworm during Kharif 2002 was low to moderate. Also there were 
mixed findings regarding its yield vis-a-vis non-Bt. variety. As such no 
inference could be drawn regarding the performance of Bt. Cotton based 
on this data. It has, therefore, been decided to evaluate its performance 
for a period of three years before coming to a final conclusion about the 
performance of Bt. Cotton. There is, therefore, presently no reason to 
reconsider the approval of these varieties granted by GEAC.

The general availability of water at the railway stations on Indian Railways 
is satisfactory. 
At all stations, water is supplied from either Railways' own sources or 
from outside sources like municipality, etc. Requirement vis-a-vis 
availability of water at various stati ons is reviewed every year ahead of 
the summer season and additional new works sanctioned for improvement/ 
augmentation of water supply at stations. A large number of works, varying

from big works like provision of radial wells to small works like provision

shedding by State Electricity Board, short supply of water by Municipalities, 
equipment breakdowns, etc. Unde r such circumstances, Railways 
endeavour to rectify the situation in co-ordination with the concerned local

Amendments in Agricultural Products and Marketing Act 
3170.  DR.T. SUBBARAMI REDDY : 
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI : 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state : 
(a) whether Government propose to bring a legislation for a change 
in the existing age old Agricultural Products and Marketing Act; 
(b) whether the existing laws have immensely benefited the middle- 
men rather than farmers for which it was actually framed; 
(c) if so, what are the main provisions of the Act that are being 
changed; and 
(d). to what extent, these changes will help farmers rather than 
middle-men? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) Organized marketing 
of agricultural commodities has been promoted in the country through a 
network of regulated markets. Most of the State Governments/Union 
Territory Administrations have enacted legislation (APMC Act) to provide 
for development of agricultural produce markets. It was envisaged that 
these markets would provide requis ite physical facilities and services 
and thereby create a competitive trad e environment offering best of the 
prices to the producers/sellers. 
An Expert Committee set up by this Ministry has reviewed the 
functioning of regulated markets and in their Report of June, 2001 pointed 
out that these markets had failed to ensu re fair play of trade practices and 
market forces and suggested several reforms measures including 
amendment to the APMC Act for development of agricultural marketing in 
the country. In this connection an inter-Ministerial Task Force set up by 
this Ministry in its Report of June, 2002 has inter alia suggested 
amendments to the State Agricultural  Produce Marketing Regulation Acts 
for promotion of competitive agricultural markets in private and cooperative 
sectors, direct marketing and contract farming programmes. 
In order to guide the State Governments/UT Administrations in the 
mplementation of the suggested legislative amendments in the APMC  ct, a 
Committee has been set up under the Chairmanship of Additional cretary in the 
Department of Agriculture and Cooperation to formulate 
57

a model legislation on agricultural marketing. The Committee is in the 
process of consulting the State Government/UT Administration for finalizing 
the Model Legislation.

AND FORESTS (SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV) : (a) and (b) As per the 
information received from various State/Union Territory Governments, about 
13.5 lakh hectare of forest land is under encroachment in the country. In 
compliance with the Supreme Court's Order, the Ministry of Environment 
and Forests have issued directions in May and October, 2002 to various 
State/UT Governments to evict the in-eligible encroachers from the forest 
lands in a time bound manner as per the guidelines issued in September, 
1990 after consultation with the States, further, State/UT Government 
have been requested to monitor the eviction process at the highest level 
and to fix responsibility for inaction on the officials. As per the reports 
received from nine States/UTs, encr oachments have been evicted from 
about 96000 hectare of-forest land so far during last one year. 
(c) and (d) Biotic pressure on fore sts increases with encroachment 
on forest lands. Though, encroachment may not be the direct and the 
main cause of extinction of animal species, however it certainly makes 
flora and fauna vulnerable for extinction. Government is committed to 
remove all ineligible encroachments from forest lands and protected area 
with the help of the State/UT Governments in accordance with the law.

3233. SHRI SATISH  PRADHAN: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:

RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR.  VALLABHBHAI RAMJIBHAI

attractive for the school children. It is also the policy of the NCERT to sell 
its text books, for classes I to VIII, at subsidized rates and recover the 
differential from the sale of books for cl asses IX-XII. It is relevant to point 
out that the prices of NCERT text books are much less than the prices of 
comparable text books published by the private publishers. It is also 
pertinent to mention that the Government of Jharkhand which has 
prescribed NCERT text books since last year has purchased all the text 
books at the prices quoted by NCERT.

be reduced, it would be possible to do so only by bringing down their

Special assistance to women belonging to 
disadvantaged sections 
3242. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: 
DR. ABRAR AHMED: 
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state : 
120 

[22 August, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
(a) whether any measures and programmes have been undertaken to 
provide special assistance to women belonging to disadvantaged sections 
such as disabled, widows, elderly women, deserted women etc.; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY. OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI JASKAUR MEENA): (a) and 
(b) Yes, Sir. The Department of Women and Child Development has taken 
various measures and launched a numb er of programmes in the areas of 
welfare and support services, training and capacity building and 
employment and income generation for women, including women belonging 
to disadvantaged sections. 
Some of the major initiatives/programmes in this regard are: 
(i) Swadhar Scheme : The Scheme covers, among others, widows 
deserted by their families and relatives and left uncared for near 
religious places where they become victims of exploitation, women 
survivors of natural disaster or women victims of terrorist/extremist 
violence who have been rendered homeless and are without any 
social or economic support, mentally challenged women (except 
for the psychotic categories wh o require care in specialized 
environment in mental hospitals) who are without any support of 
family or relatives. The objective of the Scheme is to provide the 
primary needs of shelter, f ood, clothing and care to such 
marginalized women living in diffi cult circumstances. Clinical and 
legal support and counselling are also provided. 
(ii) Short Stay Homes:  Under this Scheme, temporary shelter is 
provided to women and girls who, as a result of family tension or 
discord, are made to leave th eir homes without any means of 
subsistence and have no social protection from exploitation and 
are facing litigation on account of ma rital disputes or those who are 
victims of mental maladjustments, emotional disturbances and 
social ostracism or those who have escaped from their homes due 
to family problems including mental or physical torture and need 
shelter, psychiatric treatment a nd counselling for rehabilitation and 
readjustment in family and society. 
121 

RAJYA SABHA [22 August, 2003] 
(iii) Hostels for Working Women:  Under this Scheme, financial 
assistance is given to voluntary organizations, local bodies, 
Women's Development Corporation, educational institutions, Public 
Sector Undertakings etc. for the construction of hostels for working 
women in order to enable them to seek employment and participate 
in technical training. There is a 3% reservation of accommodation 
in the hostels constructed under the Scheme for women with 
disabilities. 
(iv) Socio-Economic Programme:  The Central Social Welfare Board 
implements the Socio-Economic Programme (SEP) which 
endeavours to provide employment opportunities on full or part- 
time basis to destitute women, widows, deserted women and 
physically handicapped women to supplement their meagre family 
income. 
(v) Besides the above, under the scheme for skill upgradation and for 
employment-cum-income generation such as 'Support to Training 
and Employment Programme (STEP)', the target group covered 
are marginalized, assetless rural women and urban poor and women 
belonging to various dispossessed groups. 
Further details in regard to the above schemes and programmes can 
be accessed at the Department's website www.wcd.nic.in. 
The National Policy for the Empowerment of Women 2001 envisages 
measures and programmes to be under taken to provide special assistance 
to disadvantaged groups of women, among others, those in extreme 
poverty, destitute women, the disabled, widows, elderly women, deserted 
women etc. 
The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing a 
number of programmes and measures  for the welfare and empowerment 
of persons with disabilities and older persons, including 
women. The details are available at that Ministry's website 
www. socialjustice. nic. in.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI 
BANDARU DATTATRAYA): (a ) Rail Passenger In surance Scheme has 
been in operation since 1.8.1994 and insures bonafide passengers against 
their death or injury in train accident s or untoward incidents as defined 
under Sections 124 and 124-A of the Railways Act 1989.The loss, damage 
etc. of luggage in train accidents/untoward incidents is not covered under

luggage is paid by the Railways.

paid for loss of life or injuries to bonafide passengers who become victims 
of rail accident or untoward incidents such as terrorist acts, violent attack, 
robbery, dacoity, rioting, shoot-out or arson by any person in or on any 
train carrying passengers, or in a waiting hall, cloak room or reservation or 
booking office or on any platform or in any place within the precincts of a 
Railway station or the accidental fa lling of any passenger from a train 
carrying passengers. 
2.The scale of compensation availabl e under this scheme is provided 
in the Railway Accidents and untoward incidents (Compensation) 
Amendment Rules, 1997. Under these rule s, the compensation in case of 
death is Rs. 4 lakhs, and in case of injuries the minimum compensation is 
Rs. 32000/- and the maximum is Rs. 4,00,000/- 
3. No compensation will, however, be payable in cases of suicide or 
attempted suicide, self-inflicted inju ry, his own criminal act, or any act 
committed in a state of intoxication or insanity or natural death or disease- 
or medical or surgical treatment  unless such treatment becomes 
necessary due to injury caused by the said 'untoward incident' 
4.The application for compensation is adjudicated by Railway Claims 
Tribunal.Twenty one Benches of this tribunal have been set up in different 
parts of the country. The decrees of the Railway Claims Tribunal are satisfied 
by the Zonal Railways after following the normal procedure.

Prediction on monsoon 
3307.  DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY: 
SHRI PARMESHWAR  KUMAR AGARWALLA: 
SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR 
SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI : 
Will the Minister of SCIENCE AN D TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian  Meteorological Department's 
predictions on monsoon rain fall this year are not correct; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that pr edictions of foreign agencies are 
correct; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the Department of Meteorology has 
failed in providing correct informati on'and right forecast of monsoon for 
the last several years; 
(d) if so, what are the main factors responsible for this; and 
(e) how Government propose to improve the work efficiency of the 
Indian agencies? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI BACHI SINGH RAWAT) : (a) No, Sir. India 
174 

[22 August, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted that the rainfall for the 
country as a whole for the month of July 2003 was likely to be 102% of 
Long Period Average (LPA) with a model error of ± 9%. The actual rainfall 
in July 2003 was 107% of LPA. Thus the Long Range Forecast of IMD 
was correct. 
IMD had also predicted that the rainfall over the country as a whole in 
the southwest monsoon season (June-September) was likely to be 98% 
of LPA with a model error of ± 4%. This forecast can be verified only after 
the end of the monsoon season. 
(b) No, Sir. International climate pr ediction centres are not always 
right in their prediction.The U.S. National Centre for Environmental 
Prediction, Washington D.C., in its seasonal prediction for June - July - 
August 2003 rainfall issued in May 2003 had indicated deficient rainfall 
over India, in that period. However, the actual rainfall over the country 
from 1 June to 6 August 2003 has been 106% of LPA. 
(c) No, Sir. From 1988 to 2001, the country has received normal 
monsoon rainfall every year and this was correctly forecast by IMD with 
its 16-parameter statistical model. Ho wever, in 2002, IMD's forecast had 
a large deviation of 20% from the actual value. 
(d) and (e) The 16-parameter model used by IMD was subjected to a 
thorough review and it Was found that some parameters had lost their 
statistical correlation with the monsoon rainfall over time. This model has 
now been replaced by an 8-parameter model which uses data upto March 
and a 10-parameter model which uses data upto June.The new parameters 
are well-correlated with the monsoon rainfall and are stable overtime. 
From this year, IMD has also adopted probabilistic models, which 
give the probability of rainfall occurring in various categories viz., drought, 
below normal, near normal, above normal and excess.

quotas on five categories of steel items with additional tariff in case the 
imports exceed the relevant quota, these measures do not apply to India, 
however, the exemption is subject to the condition that import share of 
India in a particular category should not exceed 3% of China's total import 
volume in that category.

Plight of tribals in Assam and Andamans 
SHRI BIRABHADRA SINGH (Orissa): Mr. Chairman, Sir, my Special 
Mention relates to the plight of Tribals in Assam and Andamans. 
Sir, I wish to draw the attention of  the Government to the plight of 
certain tribal communities living in Assam and Andamans. The people 
belonging to the communities like Munda, Bhumija, Orams, Santals and 
Kols, who have migrated to Assam and Andamans for a living and settled 
there as citizens, are deprived of th e benefits and status of Tribals in 
those areas. 
It is unfortunate that while the people belonging to Munda, Bhumija, 
Santals, Orams and Kols communities are enjoying the status of Tribals 
in Orissa, West Bengal and Bihar, their counterparts, kiths and kins and 
blood relations in Assam and Andamans are deprived of their Constitutional 
status as Tribals. It amounts to a serious breach of their Constitutional 
right. 
I urge upon the Government to look into this matter seriosuly, refer it 
to the Scheduled Tribes Commission for a detailed study and redress their 
age-old grievances.Thanking you.

DEMAND FOR RAISING THE WATER LEVEL OF MULLAIPERIYAR 
DAM 
SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN (Tamil Nadu): Mr. Chairman, Sir, as per 
the Press reports, the Kerala Government has enacted a new legislation 
titled "The Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation Act, 2003" on 
14th August, 2003, paving the way to enact a special legislation in future 
for decommissioning of dams in the name of safety.The State Government 
of Tamil Nadu has been demanding for restoring the water level of 
Mullaiperiyar dam to 142 feet which was Brought down to 136 feet in 
1979.The Central Government has fully endorsed the findings of the Expert 
Committee, which it has set up, that  raising the water level of the 
Mullaiperiyar dam from 136 feet to 142 feet will not endanger  the safety of 
the main dam. The Central Government has also assured the Kerala 
Government that strengthening measures will be adopted for the dam's 
safety, as suggested by the Central Water Commission. It is really 
unfortunate to know that the Kerala  Government has enacted such a law 
in a situation where the issue has been hanging fire for a long time, and 
the step taken by. the Kerala Government  will further strain the process of 
arriving at a solution between the two States on water sharing. 
In the circumstances, I would ur ge upon the Minister of Water 
Resources to kindly intervene in the matter and issue necessary directions 
to the Kerala Government to ensur e the implementation of the Expert 
Committee's findings on raising the water level of Mullaiperiyar dam to 
142 feet from the existing level immediately. Thank you. 
SHRI M.J. VARKEY MATTATHIL (Kerala): Sir, I strongly object to it. 
SHRI N. JOTHI (Tamil Nadu): You can't object to it. It is the reality.

very keen that you be in the Chair, Mr. Chairman, and I could participate 
as a Parliamentarian and as a stude nt of science because that was a

happen. Today, just an hour ago, we have bid farewell to our very, very

and as the last. It really makes me so unhappy. I think that we should find

have been nominated for their excellence by the hon. President of India

point, not at a time when there is hardly anybody in the House or the

keen to improve the participation of the Members in this House and also

interested that good subjects and the issues which are of concern to the
